text: Aaron Gordon had a strong line, but the show said it took overtime and a weak Chicago defense to get there. It does not think the game means he needs to be rostered.

Gordon had his best game in a while with 18 points on 19 shots in 33 minutes during the overtime game. The show said it will be ignoring this game because it came in an unusual overtime shootout after a long stretch of quiet lines.
Aaron Gordon started but scored one point in 24 minutes. The show said there is no reason to keep waiting on him because his role and production have slipped badly.

Gordon has played 33, 31 and 31 minutes in his last three games, so the show said its 30-minute projection may be a little light. The show said his cold shooting, including 28% from three, should turn around at some point, but it warned that the field will be heavily on him tonight expecting that bounce-back.

Aaron Nesmith keeps starting and playing about 29 to 36 minutes with Tyrese Haliburton out. The show called him a percentage killer because of his poor shooting, but it said the role keeps him streamable.
Aaron Nesmith was out on 11/23 with right foot soreness. The show guessed that the absence was related to the back-to-back.

Atlanta started Wiggins on 11/18 with Kingston Flemings out, and he played 26 minutes while RayJ Dennis played only 10 off the bench. Nickeil Alexander-Walker played 32 minutes in that game, and the show called that a role he should keep.

Wiggins has started the last two Hawks games (11/18 and 11/20) while CJ McCollum and Kingston Flemings were out, and he played 34 minutes on 11/20. The show does not think he starts over Flemings once Flemings is healthy, and it noted the Hawks do not play again until Friday, 11/27.

Wiggins moved from the bench into Atlanta's starting lineup for the last two games and played 26 and 34 minutes with both CJ McCollum and Kingston Flemings out. The show said he should be rostered as a source of threes, points, rebounds, assists and steals for as long as both players are sidelined, but not once they return.

Aaron Wiggins started for Atlanta on 11/18 and 11/20 while Kingston Flemings and CJ McCollum were both out, playing 26 and 34 minutes. With Flemings back on 11/22, Wiggins returned to the bench and played 19 minutes, and the show said his value drops a lot with only one of those guards out.
Ace Bailey started but played only 24 minutes on 11/20, his second game under 25 minutes in his last four. The show said it is not dropping him but that he is starting to frustrate.
The show said Ace Bailey should keep playing a big role for Utah until Jaren Jackson Jr. returns from his MCL tear. Bailey started and played 33 minutes on 11/22.
Ace Bailey was listed as a top-100 season-long pickup with Jaren Jackson Jr. out. Bailey played 33 minutes in his last game on 11/22.
Bailey has been a steady starter at 23 to 35 minutes while Jaren Jackson Jr. is out. The show said Jackson is still a few weeks away, so the role should hold for now.

Aday Mara started on November 18 and November 20 in a two-center lineup next to Isaiah Hartenstein, and he played 29 minutes on November 20. The show said he is earning his role now and could keep a 23 to 25 minute floor when Oklahoma City gets healthy.

Rookie center Aday Mara has played 26 to 29 minutes in each of his last three games with Chet Holmgren out 8 to 10 weeks with a small patellar tendon tear, and he had 16 points and 13 rebounds on Nov 15 and 22 points and 16 rebounds on Nov 20. The show said he has produced right away with defense, rebounding and some passing, which it did not expect this soon on a deep Thunder roster. Mara was ruled out on Nov 22 with a right shin contusion, so his status needs checking before the next game.
Aday Mara was listed as a top-100 season-long pickup with Chet Holmgren out. Mara is currently injured himself, so he is a stash for now. Mara played 29 minutes in his last game on 11/20.

The show said Oklahoma City is still without Aday Mara, Chet Holmgren and Jalen Williams for 11/25. Mara has not played since 11/20, and Holmgren is out 8 to 10 weeks with a small patellar tendon tear.

Joel Embiid was downgraded with an illness and ruled out on Nov. 23, and the show said it would not fully trust Adem Bona even if Embiid sat. Bona played only five minutes that night, and Jabari Walker started and played 20 minutes instead.
AJ Dybantsa scored 16 points on 18 shots with a high usage rate. The show said his production has been middling and his shooting has been poor.

AJ Dybantsa has started every game and played 30 to 44 minutes over his last eight games. The show said he is off his minutes limit and should play close to 40 minutes against Memphis, and it preferred him to Kyshawn George.

Dybantsa played 38 minutes and posted 23 points and 12 rebounds on 11/18 while making no threes. The show said he scores by getting to the rim and likes his 11/20 matchup against a Chicago team that it says allows the most paint points in the league.
AJ Dybantsa posted back-to-back double-doubles on 11/18 and 11/20 while playing 37 or more minutes in both games. The show said he is looking better and more comfortable.
AJ Dybantsa played 41 minutes with 20 points, 11 rebounds and seven assists. The show said the rookie is playing tons of minutes and trending up, although he has not been adding defensive stats.

The show said Dybantsa's ceiling is capped by sharing usage with Anthony Davis and Trae Young in Washington. It said he has shot poorly to start the year at about 50% true shooting but should improve because he was an above-average shooter in college.

Ajay Mitchell is questionable with a left ankle sprain, and Oklahoma City is still without Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace and Jaylin Williams at the Clippers. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has scored 26 to 31 points in each of his last four games.
Ajay Mitchell returned from a sprained ankle on November 15 after missing the November 13 game, and he started and played 27 minutes. The show called him a full start going forward.
Ajay Mitchell kept his starting job and played 31 minutes, though his production has slowed lately. The show said the job is his and he should be held.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is out Sunday against Miami with back and neck injuries, which should make Mitchell quite fantasy-relevant. Mitchell has started every game this month and played 31 and 34 minutes in his last two.

Ajay Mitchell started but played only 22 minutes, and Isaiah Hartenstein also played only 22 minutes. The show thought Oklahoma City was not fully invested in the game with several regulars out, so it would not read much into the low minutes.

Ajay Mitchell started for Oklahoma City on 11/22 with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Aday Mara out, and he took 17 shots in 22 minutes. The show said he had the expected high usage but shot poorly, and it said the rest of that short-handed Thunder game should be thrown out.
Ajay Mitchell played 35 minutes on 11/23 while Oklahoma City was short-handed. The show said he is in a bad shooting slump but expects his percentages to rise toward his expected numbers.
Al Horford sat Monday, Nov. 2, for rest on the second night of a back-to-back, not an injury, and is available Thursday.

Al Horford started over Will Richard, but he went scoreless in 14 minutes and came off the bench in the second half. Charles Bassey started the second half instead, and the show said Steve Kerr will keep mixing lineups.

Horford has started two of Golden State's last five games but has played only 13, 15, 21, 10 and 14 minutes in that span, including 14 minutes in his start on 11/16. The show said his minimum $3,500 price is the only thing making him a value, and it said it would rather see Charles Bassey or De'Anthony Melton start.

Horford came off the bench for 17 minutes on 11/19 after missing 11/18, and he has played 10 to 21 minutes in each recent game. The show said he simply cannot play big minutes at his age, which is why Charles Bassey has taken the center job.

Caruso returned on Nov. 4 after missing four games and played 20 minutes off the bench with seven points. The show said he should carve out his own role with Cason Wallace and Jalen Williams likely out for the season and Chet Holmgren sidelined.

Caruso started on Nov 11 and played 29 minutes, then came off the bench for 27 and 18 minutes in his next two games. The show said a lot of guard minutes are up for grabs in Oklahoma City, so it would hold him through a bad game.
Alex Caruso played only 9 minutes because he could not finish the game. The show said his inability to last through games is the main problem with trusting him.
Alex Karaban played 29 minutes and went scoreless while Sacramento was without Zach LaVine and De'Andre Hunter. The show called him the worst pick in his draft class.
He is questionable with left knee soreness, and Deandre Ayton started at center in his place Monday and played 24 minutes.
Alex Sarr scored 25 points with three blocks after scoring 30 points in his previous game. The show said his usage has gone up after a poor start, though his shooting will not stay this hot.
Alex Sarr (illness) and Tre Johnson (low back soreness) are questionable against Houston, which would open minutes for Bilal Coulibaly.
Alex Sarr played just 22 minutes but still posted a useful line. The show said his minutes have been all over the place this season.

Alex Sarr played only 20 minutes on 11/20 and scored three points, his second straight game near 20 minutes after he played 27 to 44 minutes in the stretch before. The show said his minutes swing back and forth and that his blocks keep his value up even in poor games.

Alex Sarr's minutes were back up to 26 on 11/22 after a couple of quiet games. The show said his minutes move around based on how he is playing and how the rotation is set, so his fantasy value rises and falls all season.

Sarr bounced back with 31.25 DraftKings points in 26 minutes after a 10.25-point game on November 20. His game-to-game swings have been large all month, and the show said he will be both a buy-low and a sell-high candidate many times this season.

Alex Sarr is in a cold stretch, playing 20 to 26 minutes as a starter in his last four games after 27 to 31 minutes in mid-November. He had 7 points in 24 minutes on 11/24. The show said he swings between hot and cold runs often and is in one of his low points now.

Allen Graves moved into the starting lineup on Nov 20 with Collin Murray-Boyles out, and he played 33 minutes with 20 points and 10 rebounds. He had also played 31 minutes on Nov 18 after Murray-Boyles left that game after five minutes, after playing 13 to 16 minutes in the games before. The show said Graves has been solid in limited minutes, with good defense and energy on the offensive glass.
Graves started over Collin Murray-Boyles on November 23, which was his second straight start, and the show said Toronto needed floor spacing. He played 31 minutes but managed only seven points.

Houston is without Clint Capela and Steven Adams, and Marcus Smart is serving a league suspension. Alperen Sengun has played 35 to 39 minutes in three of his last four games, but Houston is a 17.5-point favorite over a Utah team missing Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr.

Alperen Sengun left Wednesday's win at Indiana with a swollen right eye and a scratched left cornea. Houston did not say whether he will miss time before Friday at Denver, and Steven Adams opened the second half at center.
Sengun is questionable at Denver with an eye injury, and Clint Capela is out and Steven Adams is questionable, so Houston's center spot is the key late-slate decision.

Alperen Sengun posted a triple-double with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists in 36 minutes against Denver on November 20. The show preferred him over Joel Embiid on Monday because Sengun has the better matchup against the Clippers.

The show said Alperen Sengun has a 34% assist rate this season, well above Fred VanVleet and Reed Sheppard, which gives him real Jokic-style assist upside. The show added that Kevin Durant's presence as a second high-usage player keeps Sengun's ceiling a little lower.

The show said Houston is fully healthy for 11/25 and called Alperen Sengun one of its favorite tournament spend-ups against Phoenix. The show said it would mainly stick to Sengun, Kevin Durant and Amen Thompson from Houston.

Amen Thompson ran the point for Houston on November 15 with Fred VanVleet resting and Marcus Smart suspended, and he played 29 minutes with 26 points, seven rebounds and seven assists. The show said he is much more productive when he is the point guard, but his role has not been that this season. VanVleet returned on November 16.

Thompson returned after missing one game with soreness, and that sent Tari Eason back to the bench. The show said Thompson looks much better than he did a couple of weeks ago, though sharing the ball with Fred VanVleet limits his ceiling.
Amen Thompson played only 26 minutes, his lowest total in recent games, and the show said his dip is real. The show was less willing to buy low on him than on Kevin Durant.

The show said Amen Thompson has become a lower priority on offense with Alperen Sengun, Kevin Durant, Jabari Smith Jr., and Fred VanVleet all involved, and he has played more on the perimeter. It noted he had both a steal and a block in three of his four games before November 20, which it read as a sign his defensive stats are coming back.

The show said Houston has been cautious with Thompson's minutes since a knee injury that may still be bothering him. He has played 31, 26 and 28 minutes in his last three games, and the show was concerned about the minutes despite liking the matchup.
Amen Thompson played only 28 minutes on 11/23, and the show suspected his knee is bothering him.

Andre Drummond started at center on 11/21 with Karl-Anthony Towns out with an illness, after playing 7 to 15 minutes off the bench in his previous four games. He played 23 minutes with 13 rebounds, three blocks and a steal. The show said rebounds and blocks are why you would stream him while Towns is out.

The show said Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart are questionable and OG Anunoby is out for 11/25. The show said Andre Drummond would be the best value on the slate at $4,300 if Towns sits, and Drummond started and scored 32.25 DK points on 11/21 when Towns did not play.

Nembhard is questionable at Cleveland with a hip sprain after missing two games; Rick Carlisle said it should not be a long absence. Quenton Jackson has started in his place with Tyrese Haliburton also out.

With Tyrese Haliburton out, Nembhard played 32 minutes and posted 16 points and 8 assists along with 6 turnovers. The show said this kind of game makes him a clear play in head-to-head formats and a borderline one in roto.
Andrew Nembhard played 38 minutes on 11/23 with Tyrese Haliburton out. The show said he is mid even in that role and becomes droppable once Haliburton returns.

Giannis Antetokounmpo is out Sunday with a groin injury, which raises the question of whether Wiggins gets another decent game or Bobby Portis sees more minutes. Wiggins has played between 19 and 34 minutes off the bench this month.

Anfernee Simons scored 18 points in 26 minutes off the bench on 11/21 with Jaylen Brown out. He had started on 11/18 but returned to the bench with Tyrese Maxey back. The show said Brown's absence helped his scoring and that he is a points-and-threes streamer.

Jaylen Brown returned from his injury on November 23 and played 29 minutes, and Simons fell to 18 minutes and three points off the bench. The show said Simons is only a single-game streaming option once Brown is back.

Anfernee Simons started on 11/18 and played 38 minutes while Jaylen Brown was out, then played 26 minutes off the bench on 11/21. The show said his value is down with Brown expected back and guessed he will play only about 19 to 21 minutes.

The show said Anthony Black got a big bump while Jalen Suggs was out and with Paolo Banchero still out, and that he needs around 30 minutes a night to keep producing. Black started every game Suggs missed from October 28 to November 11, and his minutes have stayed between 33 and 37 in the four games since Suggs returned. The show doubted he keeps that workload once Orlando is fully healthy, and Banchero has not played since October 23.

Anthony Black stuffed the stat sheet on 11/20 with three steals and two blocks but turned it over five times on 11 shots. The show said his steals, blocks, rebounds and assists are running above his normal levels and may come down, possibly once Paolo Banchero returns.
Black has started and played 33 to 37 minutes a game while Paolo Banchero has been out. The show said his upside will shrink when Banchero returns but that he can still be useful.

Black has been starting and playing about 33 to 37 minutes with Paolo Banchero out. The show said his scoring and assist volume is strong but his shooting percentages have come back down, and a Banchero return is looming that could cut into his role.

Anthony Black played only 28 minutes on 11/24 after logging 33 to 39 minutes in each of his previous six games, and he scored 5 points on 8 shots. The show said he is in the slump it expected after his hot start and that his fall has been steep.
He missed Friday with his ankle sprain, and the show doubts he plays both games of the back-to-back that continues Saturday at Oklahoma City.

He has missed two straight games with his ankle sprain and is questionable again at Detroit. Kyshawn George scored 33 and 38.25 DK points in the two games without him, and the show expects George to be the most popular play if Davis sits.
Anthony Davis had 21 points and 13 rebounds in 34 minutes Wednesday, and Washington hosts Detroit on the second night of a back-to-back. The Wizards have not posted their injury report yet.

Anthony Davis re-aggravated his previously injured wrist on 11/24 and had it taped, but he did not miss time and later took the tape off. The show said it thinks he is all right, and he finished with 33 points and 13 rebounds in 37 minutes.

The show said Anthony Davis plays a lot of center because Washington keeps Alex Sarr in the mid-20s in minutes and barely plays Deandre Ayton. Ayton has played 11 minutes or fewer in each of the last seven games. The show said Davis has about a 28.9 percent usage rate with AJ Dybantsa on the floor and could draw fouls against Boston's foul-prone centers.
He is ruled out tonight.
He is ruled out tonight (arthroscopic procedure on his right knee).

Minnesota is again without Anthony Edwards, Donte DiVincenzo and Jaylen Clark against the Knicks, and Jonathan Kuminga is questionable with a right shoulder contusion. When Kuminga sat Tuesday, Trey Lyles played 31 minutes off the bench.
The show said Anthony Edwards had knee surgery and is out until sometime in January. He has not played in Minnesota's recent games.
Anthony Edwards is out again for Minnesota, along with Donte DiVincenzo and Jaylen Clark, so the Wolves lean on their bench wings and forwards against a short-handed Memphis team.
Asa Newell had surgery Tuesday to repair a plantar plate tear in his left big toe, hurt November 4. He will be re-evaluated in about four months.

Ausar Thompson played 38 minutes, his most in recent games, and his minutes have risen from 29 to 34 to 33 to 38 across his last four starts. The show credited the bigger minutes for his strong production and called him very useful in punt-points builds.

The show said Thompson has shown a ceiling lately because Detroit is missing Jalen Duren and Tobias Harris is gone, and he played 38 minutes on Sunday. It warned that those factors may not last and that his salary has climbed to $6,800.

Ausar Thompson played 31 minutes with 10 rebounds, seven assists and four blocks on just three shots. The show said he is now playing big minutes most nights, which is why his numbers have climbed so much.

Austin Reaves is ruled out at Phoenix with a left heel bruise (X-rays negative, day-to-day). Collin Sexton is questionable after stitches over his eye, while Quentin Grimes is available with a splint on his finger.
He is ruled out tonight. Grimes is the main beneficiary and could post top-70 numbers in those games.
He is questionable tonight vs UTA.

The show said the Lakers are optimistic Reaves will return on Friday, November 27, after the team's Thanksgiving break. He has not played since November 11, and the show expects Sandro Mamukelashvili to fall out of the rotation and Jake LaRavia's role to shrink once he is back.

Ayo Dosunmu started and played 34 minutes on 11/21 with Anthony Edwards and Donte DiVincenzo out, scoring 19 points with three steals. He scored only 6 points on 11/19. The show said it was good to see him get back on track.
Ayo Dosunmu was listed as a top-50 season-long pickup with Anthony Edwards out. Dosunmu played 34 minutes in his last game on 11/21.
Dosunmu has started every Minnesota game in the box scores since mid-November, playing 30 to 39 minutes with Anthony Edwards out. The show said he stays a must-start until Edwards comes back.

Bam Adebayo sat the second half Monday with right hip tightness; Miami called it proactive and does not think it is long-term. Giannis Antetokounmpo moved to center and Andrew Wiggins started the second half. Miami next plays Wednesday.

Bam Adebayo carried the Miami offense on 11/22 with Giannis Antetokounmpo out, playing 37 minutes with 24 points, 15 rebounds and 12 assists. The show said Davion Mitchell was noticeably worse in an Adebayo-centered offense than with Giannis, and Bobby Portis started but did little in 21 minutes.

Baylor Scheierman played 19 minutes and scored all eight of his points down the stretch to help seal the win. The show said he should be starting over the Hauser, Gonzalez, Walsh and Harper group, although it does not expect Mazzulla to give him 28 minutes a night.
Ben Sheppard is having surgery Wednesday to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee.
Ben Simmons is out for the season.
Bennett Stirtz played 25 minutes off the bench on Friday, Nov. 20, as Oklahoma City rallied from 16 down, and he scored back-to-back baskets during the third-quarter comeback.

Bennett Stirtz played 32 minutes and scored 21 points on Nov. 22 when Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and several other Thunder players were out. The show said he is only a deep-league option, and his minutes fell to 19 on Nov. 23 when Gilgeous-Alexander returned.

Stirtz played 32 minutes on Nov. 22 with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander out, but he fell to 19 minutes on Nov. 23 when Gilgeous-Alexander returned. The show said he was still productive in the smaller role and made a case to play him.
Bilal Coulibaly returned on Nov. 11 after missing Nov. 9 and played 25 minutes off the bench. The show said he is off the injury report and offers steals, blocks and a few assists.
The show said Coulibaly gets 23 to 25 minutes basically every night and offers steal and block upside even with low scoring. He played 26 and 24 minutes in Washington's last two games.
Bilal Coulibaly has played in the low to mid 20s in minutes for Washington. The show said his assists are lower than they should be and expects his blocks and steals to bounce back soon.
Bilal Coulibaly has played 21 to 29 minutes off the bench in six of Washington's last seven games. The show said he is playable because of his price and minutes but would go no further than that.

Bobby Portis moved into the starting lineup with Giannis Antetokounmpo out and played 21 minutes. The show said he started strongly but faded, and that he is only a low-ceiling streamer when Antetokounmpo misses time.

The show said Bones Hyland should get 16 to 20 minutes off the bench while Anthony Edwards and Jaylen Clark are out. He played 23 and 21 minutes in his two games before Monday, but only 13 minutes on Monday night. The show said his strong recent numbers will not hold long term.

Hyland played 17 minutes on 11/17 and has played between 13 and 23 minutes in each of his last four games. The show said Minnesota keeps him around 15 to 16 minutes no matter who is in or out, which makes him riskier as his price rises to $4,500.

Bones Hyland scored 7 points in 16 minutes off the bench on 11/21. He has played 13 to 17 minutes in four of his last five games. The show said three of his last four games have been poor and he does not need to be held.
Braden Smith went back to the bench on Friday, Nov. 20, when Andrew Nembhard returned, and he played only 11 minutes after starting four of the previous five games.
Braden Smith started and played 24 minutes on 11/23, which is more than Quenton Jackson got. The show said Smith's bigger role is why Jackson is being dropped.
Bradley Beal (knee) has not played yet this season and is still recovering.

The show said Brandin Podziemski will be great with Stephen Curry out. Per the show, last season he averaged 17.5 points, 6.7 rebounds and 4.9 assists per 36 minutes with Curry off the floor, and this season's smaller sample is 18.2 points and 5.7 assists per 36. The show suggested taking about 10 percent off those rates as a fair expectation.

Brandin Podziemski is starting and playing about 30 minutes a night without Stephen Curry, but he scored only 10 points on Nov. 18. The show said it expected him to break out with Curry out and called his production a disappointment.

Golden State lost 126-98 at Memphis, which was its fourth straight blowout loss without Stephen Curry, who is out with a right oblique tear. The show said Brandin Podziemski is showing how hard it is to play without the open looks Curry creates for him.
Brandin Podziemski played 38 minutes on 11/22 with Stephen Curry out. The show said he is in a shooting slump but will have to carry a big load while Curry is sidelined.

The show said Podziemski has shot about 35 percent over his last five games because he is taking harder shots without Stephen Curry. Golden State has not reached 100 points in its last five games with Curry out, scoring 85, 94, 94, 98 and 88.
The show said Brandon Ingram might be back for the Clippers' next game. His return would cut into minutes for wings like Kris Dunn, Derrick Jones Jr. and Keaton Wagler.
He is ruled out tonight (right heel surgery). Wagler becomes the second scoring option behind Garland.

Ingram made his season debut on Nov. 23 after a partial Achilles tear and started, playing 27 minutes and taking 18 shots. The show said he was also in the closing lineup, had about a 32% usage rate, and will be a usage leader on the Clippers.

Brandon Ingram is reported to make his season debut on Monday. The show expects him to be somewhat limited in his first game back, which makes his impact on Darius Garland, Max Strus and the rest of the Clippers rotation unclear for now.
Ingram made his Clippers debut on Monday after sitting out since May following heel and Achilles surgery. He started and played 27 minutes in his first game back.

He is out Monday with a hip strain, Kon Knueppel is out at least four more weeks and Dennis Schroder is out at least two weeks. Moussa Diabate is questionable, and the show named Hannes Steinbach as the fill-in if he sits.

Brandon Miller, Kon Knueppel and Dennis Schroder are all out at Phoenix, while Moussa Diabate and Grant Williams are probable. Sion James and Grayson Allen started Monday, and Allen scored 27 points with six threes.
Brandon Miller is off the injury report after missing two games with a hip strain, with Kon Knueppel and Dennis Schroder still out with hamstring strains.

Brandon Miller missed two games with a hip strain and came back on 11/15 with 5 points in 24 minutes at the Clippers. He moved up to 32 minutes and 28 points at the Lakers on 11/17 as his workload grew. The show said his shooting has been among the worst in the league but expects a hot scoring run to come.

Miller returned on November 15 after missing time following his November 6 game, and his minutes have climbed from 24 to 32 to 33 in three games back. The show said his fantasy production has been down since the return, but the rising minutes suggest he is getting back to his full workload.

The show said Miller's minutes cap appears to be gone, and his minutes have risen from 24 to 32, 33 and 35 over his last four games. He has taken 18 or 19 shots in each of his last three games, and the show called the falling price and rising minutes an elite combination.
The show said Brandon Miller's poor shooting should improve and that Kon Knueppel's eventual return from his hamstring strain will help him. It called Miller a buy-low candidate.

Brandon Williams has a mild left hamstring strain and is out at least a week. Golden State is also without Jimmy Butler III, Kristaps Porzingis, Moses Moody and Gary Payton II at Houston, which is missing Clint Capela and Steven Adams.

Brandon Williams is questionable for 11/25 with a hamstring injury, but the show said he practiced and looks likely to return. The show expects his return to push LJ Cryer out of the rotation, and Cryer has already fallen from starting to 11 or 12 minutes off the bench in his last two games.

Brayden Burries has been starting for the Bucks and playing roughly 23 to 29 minutes a night, with strong rebounding for a guard. The show said the struggling Bucks should hand more of the offense to their recent lottery pick as the season goes along, which could expand his role.

The rookie has played 25 to 29 minutes in each of his last four games, and he scored a season-high 26 points with eight rebounds against Philadelphia on November 21 even though he came off the bench that night after starting every prior game. The show said his minutes and floor are high enough that he should hold a steady role all season despite some dud games.

Burries has come off the bench in the last two games after starting earlier in the month, but he played 29 minutes on November 23. The show called him a very good rebounding guard and said his usage swings a lot from night to night, and it added that Milwaukee clearly wants to get its prized rookie more involved.

Brice Sensabaugh played the whole fourth quarter Tuesday and scored 25 of his 40 points in it as Utah pulled away from the Clippers. His bench minutes have climbed four straight games with Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. out, but Utah has not posted its report for tonight's back-to-back at the Lakers.
Brice Sensabaugh played 26 minutes off the bench on 11/20. The show said he has been playing well lately and is mainly a source of points and threes.

Sensabaugh scored 40 points in 35 minutes on 11/17, but he then played only 14 minutes on 11/18. The show said his minutes, which had been trending toward 30, fell back down and that the Jazz have a quick leash on him.

Brice Sensabaugh played only 17 minutes as Svi Mykhailiuk took over the bench scoring role. The show said Sensabaugh's minutes depend on his shooting, since he plays when he hits shots and sits when he does not, and his recent minutes have swung between 14 and 35.

The show said Brice Sensabaugh is a bench scorer who should keep getting minutes for as long as Lauri Markkanen is out with a right hand fracture. He has been inconsistent since his 40-point game on 11/17, playing 14 to 26 minutes in the four games since.

Brook Lopez is starting at center for the Clippers and scored 23 points with five threes against San Antonio on November 19. The show said he has scored 20 or more in five of his last seven games and is giving early-round fantasy value.

Brook Lopez scored 21 points in 25 minutes as the Clippers' starting center, his fourth game of 20 or more points in his last six. The show said he is having a full resurgence this season and should be held even with Yanic Konan Niederhauser emerging.

The show said Lopez's fantasy value is gone because the Clippers are splitting center minutes among several bigs, including Isaiah Jackson. Lopez started but played only 21 minutes on Nov. 23, and the show expects him to be traded.

The show cited a report that contending teams are calling the Clippers about Lopez, likely as a bench player. It said a Lopez trade or injury would open the center minutes for Yanic Konan Niederhauser.

Buddy Hield moved into the Bulls starting lineup in place of the injured Norman Powell on Nov. 22 and scored 33 points in 40 minutes after coming off the bench in his previous five games. He started again on Nov. 23 with Powell still out, and the show said it liked his game but viewed Svi Mykhailiuk as the safer role.
Hield has started the last two games with Norman Powell out, playing 40 and 27 minutes. The show said Chicago needs his spacing without Powell and that he will keep shooting a lot of threes.

Hield started Sunday with Norman Powell and Caleb Wilson out and played 40 minutes in an overtime loss to Denver. Chicago hosts Cleveland on the second night of a back-to-back, and its report was not filed this morning.

Hield moved into the starting lineup on 11/22 and 11/23 with Norman Powell out, after coming off the bench for about 19 to 25 minutes before that. He played 40 minutes and scored 33 points with seven threes on 11/22. The show said his defense limits him and it expects him closer to 24 or 25 minutes while Powell is out.
Jalen Duren (hamstring) and Isaiah Joe (hip) are both ruled out at Miami. Cade Cunningham played 48 minutes Thursday and scored 52 points, and Paul Reed played 38 minutes at center.

Cade Cunningham returned on 11/20 after he missed the Pistons' 11/18 game and played 36 minutes. The show said there was never much concern about the knee and that the missed game was more of a night off.

Cunningham picked up two fouls in the first quarter and a third early in the second on Sunday, Nov. 22, so he played only 14 first-half minutes while also playing through right knee soreness. He leaned into setting up teammates against Dyson Daniels' defense, and J.B. Bickerstaff said before the game that protecting him was the most important thing.

Cade Cunningham scored only 5 points with a usage rate the show put at about 20 percent and no free-throw attempts, but he still had 15 assists. The show called it a fluky bad shooting night rather than a change in role.
Cade Cunningham missed the 11/24 game at Orlando with right knee soreness after playing 33 minutes on 11/22. The show said it is betting he plays in Detroit's next game.
Caleb Martin started on Saturday, November 21, because P.J. Washington sat out with an illness, the first game Washington has missed this season. Martin played 20 minutes.
Caleb Martin played 29 minutes as a starter on Nov. 22 with P.J. Washington out and posted 13 points with four steals. The show credited Washington's absence for opening up that big game.

Caleb Martin's minutes as a Dallas starter have gone 33, 34, 20, 20 and 29 over his last five games. The show said his minutes seem to depend on how well he is playing at the time, which makes him hard to predict.

Caleb Martin kept starting and played 30 minutes with five steals and two blocks. The show said his shooting this season is far above his career norms and his steal rate is unsustainable, and it noted he is not guaranteed 25 minutes a night.
The show said Caleb Wilson is out again on 11/25. He has not played since 11/11, and the show said Isaac Okoro and Patrick Williams pick up some of his role.
Cam Johnson was out on Oct. 28 and is expected to return fairly soon.

Cam Spencer has started every game since Ty Jerome got hurt after November 13, playing 27 to 34 minutes as a starter. He averaged about 18 points and eight assists over the three starts before November 19, then posted 11 assists in 27 minutes on November 19 with Jerome out again. The show said Spencer should be held even after Jerome returns to see how the roles shake out.
Cam Spencer was listed as a top-75 season-long pickup because Ty Jerome is out, which opens up minutes for him. Spencer played 27 minutes in his last game on 11/19.

Spencer played 30 minutes off the bench on November 21 with Cameron Boozer out, while Ty Jerome played 27 minutes in his first game back. The show said Boozer's absence gives Spencer more runway, and he followed with 24 points in 21 minutes on November 23 with Boozer still out.

Spencer has come off the bench in the last two games after starting the four before that, but he scored 24 points in 21 minutes on November 23 with Cameron Boozer out. The show listed him as a likely beneficiary while Boozer misses about four weeks.

Cameron Boozer made seven threes and scored 29 points on 11/16, but he played only 29 minutes because Memphis was comfortably ahead. The show said he normally settles into a 32 to 33 minute role and liked him against Cleveland with Evan Mobley out and Ty Jerome out on his own side.

With Ty Jerome out on Monday, Cameron Boozer took on more of the scoring and set a season high with 29 points, making 7 of 13 threes, including two during the 10-0 third-quarter run that tied the game.
Boozer has played 29, 29 and 28 minutes in his last three games, including competitive ones. The show said the minutes cap is frustrating but that he still has a strong ceiling and floor at $8,400.

Memphis is short again at Cleveland: Ty Jerome (right hip) and Isaiah Stewart (illness) are out, and GG Jackson had foot surgery Tuesday and will be re-evaluated in about three months. Boozer, Cam Spencer and Jerami Grant carry more of the load.

The show said Cameron Boozer's playmaking has taken a step forward and that he looks comfortable in Memphis's system. He has started all 16 games, averaging about 31 minutes with roughly nine rebounds and five assists per game. The show called him a triple-double threat, though his only double-digit assist game so far came on October 29.
He is ruled out tonight (right ankle sprain).

The show said Cameron Boozer is out at least four weeks. He has already missed Memphis's games on 11/21 and 11/23. The show said no one on the roster is likely to become a full-time replacement for his role.
Boozer is expected to miss at least a month with a sprained right ankle. Ty Jerome took 21 shots in 29 minutes in the first game without him.
Cameron Johnson picked up five fouls and still played 27 minutes, but he had nine points and no rebounds. The show said to move on from him.

Cameron Johnson took 13 shots and scored 19 on 11/20, a night when Jamal Murray had an off game. The show said he usually takes about nine or 10 shots and would only become a must-roster player if 13 shots became normal, so it treats this as one game to watch.

Johnson played 36 minutes in an overtime game but took only 9 shots. The show said it keeps hoping for consistency from him, but that low shot volume in an extra-period game is not a good sign. It named Jamal Murray, Nikola Jokic and Christian Braun as Denver's only safe fantasy starters.

Cameron Johnson took 15 shots in 34 minutes against Dallas on 11/24, one of his highest shot totals in recent games. The show said he did not pay off in fantasy but is near the top of its watch list in case his bump in offensive role is real.
LeVert played for the first time this season on Wednesday and scored eight points in eight minutes. He is another name in a crowded Milwaukee guard rotation.
Caris LeVert played the final 11 minutes of the November 19 game and was in Milwaukee's closing lineup. The show could not explain the choice, which adds to the Bucks' rotation chaos.

Carter Bryant played 13 minutes on November 19 with Dylan Harper out, after 2 and 5 minutes in the two games before. The show said he was the Spurs' first player off the bench in that game, which gives him more minutes upside.
Carter Bryant played 12 scoreless minutes on 11/23. The show said he has fallen out of the rotation at times this season.
The show said Wallace is presumably out for the season. He has not played since Oct. 25.

Cedric Coward played 25 minutes in a 28-point win against GSW on Thursday, 5 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 11 minutes of garbage time. His 36.0 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.
The show said Cedric Coward's breakout season continues and it is not sure it is cooling off. He had 19 points with five threes on November 19 and has scored 18 or more in four straight games.

The show said Cedric Coward has nearly doubled his steals and blocks from last season in about the same minutes and is playing at a top-50 level. He has started every recent game, and he played 30 minutes on November 21 with Cameron Boozer out because of a right ankle sprain.
The show said Cameron Boozer's injury locks in Coward's rebounding role, which has already been strong this season. He played 30 minutes and grabbed nine boards on November 23.
Coward has been held to about 30 minutes a game even while producing well. The show said his rebounding looks sustainable, but his limited minutes cap how much better he can get.

The show said Coward's price jumped because the pricing is accounting for Cameron Boozer being out. He has taken 15 and 16 shots in his last two games while playing 30 minutes in each, and the show called him fine but expensive.

Chaney Johnson scored 10.0 of his 10.0 DraftKings points in garbage time of a 30-point loss against CHI on Wednesday, when the lead was 20 or more late. His line is bigger than his normal role; expect less in a close game.

Charles Bassey has started Golden State's last three games (11/18, 11/19 and 11/22) and played 22, 25 and 26 minutes after mostly playing 11 to 20 minutes off the bench before that. The show called him a possible new starting center because Golden State has few good center options, and it noted his next game is Wednesday, 11/25. The show said Steve Kerr's rotations make the role risky.
Charles Bassey has moved into the Warriors' starting lineup and started on 11/22. The show said he was one of the most-added players and is worth grabbing while that role lasts.

Chaz Lanier played 25 minutes on Tuesday only because Detroit was missing Ronald Holland II and Duncan Robinson, and he scored just 3 points. The show said his minutes should mostly disappear as injured players return.
He is ruled out tonight. Mara had 11 points, 10 rebounds and two blocks in 20 minutes Monday with Holmgren out.
Holmgren remained out Wednesday against Atlanta. Isaiah Hartenstein grabbed 17 rebounds in his place.

Chris Cenac Jr. jumped into the rotation for 12 minutes with Neemias Queta resting. The show said he looked very athletic and that Joe Mazzulla talked him up after the game, so he is someone to keep in mind.

Chris Cenac Jr.'s minutes have climbed from 7 to 12 to 17 over the Celtics' last three games. The show said Joe Mazzulla could try big lineups with Cenac starting next to Paul George and Jayson Tatum, because Jordan Walsh played only 4 minutes after starting on November 18 and Baylor Scheierman's minutes have fallen to around 10 to 18.
The show thinks Chris Youngblood will be out a while longer. He has a right heel contusion and has not played in Portland's recent games.

Christian Anderson has played 18, 14, 21 and 25 minutes off the bench over his last four games, and he scored 25 points with six threes in 25 minutes on 11/23 while Kon Knueppel, Dennis Schroder and Grayson Allen were all out. The show said the hot shooting will not stick, but it wants to see whether his role settles at 20 or 25 minutes. Grayson Allen is questionable for 11/25, and the show said the returns of Allen, Knueppel and Schroder would all cut into Anderson's minutes.

Christian Anderson scored 25 points in 25 minutes off the bench while Charlotte was without Kon Knueppel, Dennis Schroder and Grayson Allen. The show said he will not shoot like that every night and should be treated as a one-game spike.

Christian Braun has played 28 to 37 minutes in Denver's recent games. The show said it trusts his minutes no matter what and that his production last season tracked how his injured ankle felt, so a healthy Braun should be a top-100 player in roto formats.
Christian Braun had four steals on 11/20 and has been running a very high steal rate this season. The show expects the steals to come back down and his value to slip with them.
Christian Braun has locked up a starting role with 31 to 38 minutes in recent games. The show said he has taken minutes away from DeMar DeRozan.

Braun is playing about 34 minutes a game as a Denver starter, up from about 32 last season. The show said his steals have roughly tripled to about 2.2 per game and that this spike, along with hot two-point shooting, is inflating his rankings.

Christian Braun played 29 minutes and kept producing with 15 points, a steal and a block. The show said his steal rate and shooting are likely to come down, but it still thinks he should be rostered everywhere.

CJ McCollum moved back into Atlanta's starting lineup on November 15 with Kingston Flemings out with a lumbar back issue, and he played 30 minutes. He scored 20 points with four steals, and the show said he went nine for nine at the free-throw line. The show treated Flemings as day-to-day.

The show said McCollum is out about a month. He had been playing a sixth-man scoring and ball-handling role off the bench, and the show said he volunteered for that role so Kingston Flemings could play with the starters. His last game was Nov 15.
Capela started on Oct. 30 with Alperen Sengun and Steven Adams out, but he is now out himself. He missed Nov. 2 with a right ankle sprain.

White played 16, 18 and 16 minutes in his first three games and then 20 minutes in each of his next three. He scored 21 points on November 15 even with Brandon Miller and Naz Reid playing. The show said it is waiting for his minutes to rise to around 24 before trusting him at $5,400.

White played 26 minutes on 11/17 after being held to 20 minutes in each of his previous two games. The show said Charlotte has been careful with White and Brandon Miller because of their injury histories, and it expects White to have a big role going forward.

Charlotte has ramped up Coby White's minutes slowly since his return, from 16, 18 and 16 minutes in his first three games to 20 minutes in three straight and then 26 minutes on 11/17. He scored 21, 21 and 19 points in those last three games despite the cap. The show said his usage is through the roof and that he is starting to look like himself again.

Coby White played 26 minutes on November 20 and finished one assist short of a double-double with 17 shot attempts, losing some minutes to a blowout. The show said Charlotte's shots are concentrated on White, Brandon Miller and Naz Reid, and it called White underpriced at $5,700 even against a strong Memphis defense.

Coby White has started for Charlotte and played 28 minutes on 11/23, up slightly from 26 in each of the two games before. The show said he is too cheap at $5,900 in a good matchup and is best if Grayson Allen stays out.

Coby White has been playing 20 to 26 minutes as a starter while posting a 34% usage rate and a 39% assist rate. The show said a projection of about 24 to 25 minutes is fair, which keeps his minutes as the main limit on his ceiling.

Cody Williams started for Minnesota on 11/17 and played 13 minutes after logging between 2 and 7 minutes off the bench in his earlier games. The show said he becomes interesting in deep leagues only if Minnesota keeps starting him.
Cody Williams started on November 17 while Jonathan Kuminga was out, but he did not play at all on November 19 once Kuminga returned. He has no role when Minnesota's forwards are healthy.

Collin Gillespie played 27 minutes off the bench on November 20. The show believes Phoenix already sees him as its starting point guard of the future and said a Dejounte Murray trade would not help anyone on the Suns.

Gillespie played 30 minutes off the bench on November 23, but the show pointed out that overtime added about five of those minutes. It said he has averaged about 23 to 25 minutes over the last two weeks as the one bench player Phoenix trusts in the offense. It added that he would become a clear start if Devin Booker, Jalen Green, Miles Bridges or Dillon Brooks missed time.
Gillespie's bench minutes have climbed from 17 to 27 to 30 over his last three games. The show said his minutes have trended way up while Phoenix keeps winning.
Collin Murray-Boyles returned on Nov. 11 and started, playing 20 minutes after missing Nov. 9. The show expects him to be available Thursday.
Collin Murray-Boyles started at center over Jakob Poeltl on Sunday and played 40 minutes, including all of overtime, while Scottie Barnes returned from a four-game groin absence with 36 minutes.

Murray-Boyles came off the bench for 24 minutes after starting Toronto's games on November 15, 17 and 18. Jakob Poeltl has now started three straight games, and the show said Toronto seems to be choosing starters by matchup. The show said to start both Poeltl and Murray-Boyles when Poeltl starts, but only Murray-Boyles when he is the one starting.

Murray-Boyles is probable to return from the concussion protocol against Milwaukee, which likely sends Allen Graves back to a bench role. Kawhi Leonard and RJ Barrett are still out, keeping Scottie Barnes at the center of the offense.

Sexton has averaged 14.2 points over his last five games through Nov. 17 while coming off the bench, and the show tied the bump to Austin Reaves being out. His minutes have stayed in the 20 to 27 range in that stretch. His role should shrink once Reaves returns.
Collin Sexton played 18 minutes off the bench on 11/20. The show said he is only a streaming option on a favorable slate.
The show said the Dallas coach told the media that Cooper Flagg gets lazy on defense when his shots are not falling. The show liked Flagg under $10,000 and hoped the comment fires him up.
Flagg played 36 minutes on Saturday with P.J. Washington out and Dallas has a back-to-back at Utah on Sunday. He went 7 of 13 at the foul line, the first time he has missed six free throws in a game.
Dallas is without Dereck Lively II, and P.J. Washington and Walter Clayton Jr. are questionable. The Clippers are missing Bradley Beal and Brandon Ingram.

Corey Kispert played 16 minutes off the bench on November 15 while Luguentz Dort played 18 and Aaron Wiggins played 24. The show said the wing minutes will keep rotating among Dort, Wiggins and Kispert and that Dorian Finney-Smith has not really been in the rotation.
Corey Kispert scored 18 points in 19 minutes off the bench with a usage rate the show put at 26 percent. The show said he has not been good this season and is at most a three-point streamer.
The show said Oklahoma City waived Dalen Terry a few days after signing him, as part of the move to get Nique Clifford. Terry played five and six minutes in his two games with the Thunder.
He played 37 minutes Friday, and the show labeled him and Robert Williams III doubtful for Saturday against San Antonio on the back-to-back.
Lillard played both games of the back-to-back against the Thunder, scoring 18 points in 32 minutes on the second night. The show said his usage is not as high as expected.
Damian Lillard played 31 minutes on the second night of the back-to-back Tuesday, up from 24 Monday, when Portland emptied its bench late.

With Deni Avdija out on 11/17, Lillard took 19 shots in 31 minutes and scored 25 points. The show said he had a team-leading 33.5% usage rate without Avdija and that Portland may have held his minutes down because it was the second leg of a back-to-back.

Portland plays Minnesota again on the second night of a back-to-back, and the Blazers had not posted their injury report Tuesday morning. Lillard played only 24 minutes Monday after Portland emptied its bench down 19 late.

The show said Ja Morant's absence has opened up more of the offense for Damian Lillard, Jrue Holiday, and Scoot Henderson. Morant is out at least four weeks with a left hamstring strain, and the show added that Portland will probably rest Lillard at some point this season.

The show said Damian Lillard is still shooting below expectation as he returns from his Achilles injury and that it should improve as the season goes on. He played only 29 minutes on 11/23 in a comfortable win.

Daniel Gafford started at center and played 31 minutes on 11/21, up from 17 to 24 minutes in his previous three games, with Dereck Lively II out after right foot surgery. He had 10 points, 10 rebounds, two steals and a block. The show said 31 minutes as the starting center is enough to hold him.

Daniel Gafford played 31 and 28 minutes in the two games P.J. Washington missed, after 24 minutes on Nov. 18 with Washington active. The show believes the jump is mostly tied to Washington's absence rather than a permanent move to 25-plus minutes.

Daniel Gafford played 27 minutes as the starting center even with P.J. Washington back, and Dereck Lively II remains out after foot surgery. The show had been watching whether he would be a 22-minute or 25-plus-minute player, and it said this answer makes him a hold.

Detroit came back from 14 down to end San Antonio's 12-game winning streak with Kevin Huerter starting for Duncan Robinson and Ausar Thompson running more offense. Detroit plays at New Orleans on the second night of a back-to-back and has not posted its injury report.

Jenkins has started and played 36 to 39 minutes in each of the last four Pistons games with Jalen Duren out with a right hamstring strain. The show said that when Duren returns, it expects Jenkins to keep starting over John Collins.

Jenkins has started six straight games for Detroit and has played between 35 and 42 minutes in each of them. The show said he is playing well enough that he should be rostered in every league until his minutes drop.
Daniss Jenkins played 38 minutes as a starter with Jalen Duren out. The show expects Jenkins to keep starting even after Duren returns, which might happen this week, though no update has come out.

Jenkins has started and played about 38 minutes a game over his last seven games, topping out at 42. The show said he is near the league lead in minutes over the last three weeks and that the workload makes him worth using even if his production cools.
Daniss Jenkins was listed as a top-75 season-long pickup with Jalen Duren out. Jenkins played 38 minutes in his last game on 11/22.

Jenkins has started every recent Detroit game and played 35 to 39 minutes. The show said he could stay in the lineup even after Jalen Duren returns if Detroit moves John Collins to the bench and plays small with Ausar Thompson at the four, though Jenkins is the other candidate to go back to the bench.

Daniss Jenkins played 35 minutes with 10 assists while Cade Cunningham sat, after 38 minutes on 11/22. The show said his heavy-minutes run continues and put his usage at about 30 percent with Cunningham out.

Danny Wolf moved into the starting lineup on 11/20 when Egor Demin was benched, and he scored 20 points in 26 minutes. The show called him risky because his minutes could range from 15 to 30. It said Wolf could go back to the bench if Brooklyn starts both Demin and Mikel Brown Jr.

Wolf returned to the Nets' starting lineup on Nov. 20 and scored 20 points with four threes in 26 minutes after two bench games of 11 and 23 minutes. The show said his value depends on starting and playing close to 30 minutes, and his floor is very low when he does not.

Danny Wolf has started Brooklyn's last two games over Egor Demin, who moved to the bench after starting on 11/16 and 11/18. Wolf has made seven threes across those two starts. The show said everything is falling for him right now, but it does not buy him as a long-term player.

The show said Darius Acuff Jr. has a complete green light and that his usage and minutes will be through the roof all season. He has started all 15 games, averaging about 37 minutes and nearly 23 shot attempts per game. The show warned his efficiency can hurt some nights, but the volume is what drives his value.

The show said Walker Kessler's rim protection could take away Darius Acuff's drives and turn him into a jump shooter against the Lakers. Acuff scored 18 points in 36 minutes against Los Angeles on November 20 after scoring 36 on November 18.

Rookie Darius Acuff Jr. is getting a huge share of Sacramento's usage, playing about 37 minutes per game and averaging about 25 points and 7 assists in the box scores. The show said his efficiency is not there yet, but the volume of his role has him near the top 10 in the league in points and assists.
The show said the Kings are building their season around Acuff even at the cost of upsetting Domantas Sabonis and Zach LaVine. It expects his large role to continue as long as he stays healthy.
The show said Darius Acuff Jr.'s usage has come down, with two of his last three games under 25% usage. He played 33 minutes on 11/23.

Garland played 35 to 37 minutes in each of his last two games and scored at least 41 DraftKings points in three of his last four. The show said his minutes and production have risen as the Clippers have played more competitive games and won more often.

Darius Garland scored 27 points with seven assists while Brandon Ingram remained out after heel surgery. The show said it would like more usage from him during Ingram's absence and that his turnovers have been high.

The show said no Clipper plays big minutes, with Darius Garland the leader at 33 minutes per game and Rui Hachimura next at 29. The box scores match, with Garland at 33.2 and Hachimura at 29.0 minutes per game. The show said this makes a large minutes load for a returning Brandon Ingram unlikely.

The show said Utah does not help off, which is good for high-usage guards and bad for shooters, and called the Nov. 17 game one of the best Darius Garland spots he will get. Garland has played 35 and 37 minutes as a starter in his last two games. The show also liked Keaton Wagler as a sneaky value after he played 28 minutes off the bench on Nov. 15.

Darius Garland has played 35, 30 and 35 minutes in his last three games with Brandon Ingram out, and he scored 23 points on November 19. The show said Garland is finally playing more like it expected and hopes the run lasts more than three games.

Darius Garland played 35 minutes and took a team-high 17 shots while committing only one turnover. The show said his high turnovers have been the main problem this season and that his steals should climb back toward normal. The show also worried that the losing Clippers could give him rest days.

Garland kept a full role in Brandon Ingram's return on Nov. 23, playing 34 minutes and taking 21 shots. The show said Ingram's presence should not hurt Garland and may make defenses less focused on him.

Darryn Peterson has played 33 or 34 minutes in each of Utah's last three games as a starter while Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. are out. The show said it really likes both Peterson and Keyonte George on Nov. 17 and expects George to play in the low 30s in minutes.
Peterson played only 19 minutes because he picked up four fouls, after playing at least 31 minutes in each of his previous four games. The show said he is in a funk but it is not too worried.

The show said injuries on Utah have opened up more usage and more minutes for Darryn Peterson. He has started all 17 games and has played 31 to 35 minutes in most recent games. The show added that rookie guards usually improve over the second half of the season.

Davion Mitchell has been Miami's starting point guard and has scored 41 or more DraftKings points in three straight games, including 16 points, 10 assists and 4 steals against Houston on 11/16. The show said he does it every night and is still priced at $7,000.

Mitchell scored 24 points with six assists and six threes in 36 minutes. The show said his minutes, usage and responsibility have been far beyond what it expected, and it does not see him as a sell-high, though his shooting is well above his expected points.

The show said Davion Mitchell has become a high-minute lead ball handler next to Giannis Antetokounmpo instead of being pushed aside, and it called him the favorite for Most Improved Player. He has played 32 to 39 minutes in each of his last five games with six to 17 assists. The show expects his three-point percentage to come down but thinks the minutes and assist role can hold.

The show said Davion Mitchell has settled in as the secondary scorer and lead facilitator behind Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo on a thin Miami roster. He has started all 15 games and averaged about 35 minutes with roughly nine assists per game. The show said Erik Spoelstra clearly trusts him and that his minutes and usage look locked in.

Mitchell had his first poor game of the season in 34 minutes with Giannis Antetokounmpo out. The show said the dip made sense because the team dynamic was totally different without Giannis, and it is not worried about him.

Day'Ron Sharpe played only 25 minutes on 11/16 because of foul trouble. The show said not to worry about it and that Sharpe has settled into a steady role alongside Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr.
Day'Ron Sharpe started and played 26 minutes on 11/20. The show said no one is threatening his minutes, though the assist numbers he posted early in the season have tapered off.
The show said Day'Ron Sharpe has been piling up assists, with seven on 11/23, and is 70th over the last two weeks.

De'Aaron Fox (left hip soreness) and Devin Vassell are questionable for San Antonio against Golden State, and Tobias Harris is out. Dylan Harper had 18 points and 10 assists in 36 minutes Wednesday and would handle more of the offense if Fox sits.
De'Aaron Fox returned to the starting lineup Tuesday after missing Sunday's game and played 34 minutes, and he was on the floor to close the game.

The show said Fox has been the fourth option in San Antonio's usage behind Wembanyama, Harper and Castle. With Harper's groin injury, the show expected Fox and Castle to gain the most. It noted that when Fox himself missed a game, the streamers did not gain much because his usage is not that high.
De'Aaron Fox missed Sunday's game but is not on San Antonio's injury report tonight. Tobias Harris (calf) is likely out until early December.
De'Aaron Fox did not take on more work in the first game without Dylan Harper, taking only five shots in 32 minutes. The show said this was odd but not a long-term worry.

The show said Fox has been on the injury report for most of the season with minor issues and wondered if San Antonio is managing him early. He still played 32 minutes on 11/19, so this is a risk to watch rather than an absence.
De'Aaron Fox was ruled out of Monday's game at Sacramento with a shin injury.

De'Andre Hunter played 37 minutes on 11/20 as every Kings starter played at least 36 minutes. The show said Sacramento is pumping a lot of minutes into Hunter and is running a top-heavy rotation that is easy to project.

Hunter has been a heavy-minutes starter for Sacramento, logging 37 and 41 minutes in his last two games while scoring 30 and 20 points. The show called his workload elite and said that kind of playing time makes him worth rostering even though his scoring can be inconsistent.

Hunter has played between 35 and 41 minutes in each of his last four games. He had eight assists on November 23, which the show called extraordinarily unusual for a player who averages about two. The show said he is on a short heater and his normal line is closer to 15 points and four rebounds.

Melton has moved between the bench and the starting lineup since Stephen Curry went down, with 18 to 26 minutes in recent games and a start on Nov. 19. The show said Golden State has looked like a complete mess without Curry, so his recent games say little about his role.

De'Anthony Melton has started Golden State's last two games, playing 25 and 27 minutes, but he scored only two points on 11/22. The show said he has shot about 27 percent over the last two weeks and expects that to improve, and it believes he keeps the starting job even if Brandon Williams returns.
De'Anthony Melton's role is worth watching with Stephen Curry out. Melton played 27 minutes in his last game on 11/22.

Melton has started the last two Golden State games with Stephen Curry out, playing 25 to 27 minutes. The show said he has been ice cold from the field but his steals and assists are still there, Curry is out a few more weeks, and 27 minutes of Melton has historically been enough for solid value.

Dean Wade played 35 minutes off the bench on November 15 with Joel Embiid out. The show said everyone else on Philadelphia got more usage without Embiid but Wade did not, and that he does not reach fantasy value no matter how many minutes he plays.
Dean Wade played 35 minutes off the bench with Joel Embiid out, but he took only 5 shots. The show said his ultra-low usage makes sustained value almost impossible even when the minutes are there.

Wade started with LeBron James out and played 32 minutes with 11 rebounds. The show said Wade is generally the next man up when James sits. It also said he is a much better real-life player than a fantasy player.

Dejounte Murray has not played since 11/11, and the show said New Orleans shut him down about four days ago amid trade talk. The show cited reports that teams expect the Pelicans to attach draft assets in a deal, and it noted the Suns were linked but have denied interest. The show guessed he could be out about a month.
Dejounte Murray remains away from the team. The show cited Jake Fischer reporting that Murray views Phoenix as an attractive landing spot and that Phoenix wants a more viable big man.

Dejounte Murray was ruled out on November 20 with a left ankle sprain and has missed five straight games. The show said it believes he will never play another game for the Pelicans and may be hard to trade. That is the show's opinion, and the official reason for his absence is the ankle sprain.

The show said Murray is being held out by New Orleans while the team and his camp argue over a trade, and that there is no return date; the team's injury report lists him out with a left ankle sprain. The show said reports have the Pelicans refusing to attach a pick to move him and expects a trade before February. He has not played since Nov 11.
DeMar DeRozan played 22 minutes off the bench on 11/20 after he played 25 minutes on 11/18. The show said it is good to see him getting more involved over his last couple of games.

The show said DeMar DeRozan's minutes are down because Christian Braun has run away with the minutes at that spot. Braun has started every game and played 31 to 38 minutes lately, while DeRozan played 18 minutes on Nov. 22.

DeMar DeRozan scored four points in 18 minutes off the bench. The show said Denver's starters produced nearly all of the team's scoring and that no Nuggets bench player, including DeRozan, is worth fantasy interest.
DeMar DeRozan played 17 minutes off the bench. The show said he is done as a fantasy option and that it would take multiple injuries for his role to grow.
Deni Avdija scored 27 points and is ranked 21st over the last two weeks. The show said Ja Morant's absence and Shaedon Sharpe being out funnel more usage to him.
Portland lists Deni Avdija and Toumani Camara (abdominal soreness) as questionable at Milwaukee, with Ja Morant, Shaedon Sharpe, Vit Krejci and Robert Williams III (rest) out.

Deni Avdija is questionable with a left foot contusion after missing two straight games, and Portland is still without Ja Morant, Shaedon Sharpe and Vit Krejci. Jayson Kent started both games Avdija missed.

Avdija scored 31 points on 19 shots in a win over Philadelphia on November 23. The show said the loss of Ja Morant, who is out at least four weeks with a hamstring strain, has helped Avdija's role a bit.
He is ruled out tonight (left hamstring strain).
The show said Dennis Schroder is out for 11/25. He has not played since 11/04.
Dereck Lively II remains out with a broken foot. The show said it had seen nothing suggesting he is close to returning.
